extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, recipients, research administrators, and institutional officials responsible for compliance
extracted.subtask_short: NIH grant award terms and conditions
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, statutory restrictions, and administrative requirements that govern NIH grants and cooperative agreements, including award formation (Notice of Award), allowable uses of funds, reporting and disclosure obligations, and mandatory organizational policies. Useful for institutions administering NIH-funded projects and PI/administrative staff ensuring compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must establish safeguards to prevent employees, consultants, governing board members, and others involved in grant-supported activities from using positions for private financial gain or appearing to do so; safeguards must be reflected in written standards of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards need not be separate for grant activities if existing standards cover grant activities and are consistent with State/local law. At minimum they must address expected conduct regarding financial interests, gifts/gratuities/favors, nepotism, political participation, bribery, and must: (1) address when outside activities/relationships/financial interests are proper or improper; (2) provide for advance notification of outside activities/relationships/financial interests to a responsible official; (3) include a process for notification and review of potential/actual violations; (4) specify nature of penalties the recipient may impose (in addition to NIH/Federal penalties). Recipients need not submit standards to NIH but must make a copy available to officers, employees/consultants on the project, governing board members, and upon request to NIH. Recipients are responsible for enforcing standards, taking action on infractions, and for financial conflict of interest (FCOI) must notify NIH by submitting FCOI report via eRA Commons FCOI Module. Recipients must promptly report potential criminal violations (e.g., misappropriation of Federal funds) to HHS OIG. If PD/PI or senior/key personnel are suspended/separated, recipient must request prior approval for replacements as specified in Prior Approval Requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text Messaging While Driving (Executive Order 13513)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH encourages contractors, subcontractors, and grant/cooperative agreement recipients/subrecipients to adopt and enforce policies banning text messaging while driving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies should ban reading/entering data into handheld or other electronic devices while operating company-owned, government-owned, or personally-owned vehicles when on official Government business or performing work for the Government. NIH encourages new rules/programs, reevaluation of existing programs, and education/awareness/outreach to employees; initiatives should encourage voluntary compliance off duty. Definitions: 'Texting/Text Messaging' = reading or entering data into any handheld/other electronic device (SMS, e-mail, instant messaging, navigational info, other electronic data retrieval/communication). 'Driving' = operating a motor vehicle on an active roadway with motor running, including temporarily stationary in traffic; does not include safely pulled over and halted off an active roadway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trafficking in Persons award term (TVPA Section 106(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: For awards to private entities, the agency may terminate the award, without penalty, if the recipient or subrecipient engages in certain trafficking-related conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination authority applies if during the award the recipient/subrecipient: (a) engages in severe forms of trafficking in persons; (b) procures a commercial sex act; or (c) uses forced labor in performance of the award or subawards. This implements Section 106(g) of the Trafficking Victims Protection Act and related interim/final guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: USA PATRIOT Act biological agent restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The USA PATRIOT Act amends criminal penalties and access restrictions for possession of certain biological agents, toxins, or delivery systems if not reasonably justified by prophylactic, protective, bona fide research, or other peaceful purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricted persons (as defined by the Act) may not possess, ship, transport, or receive any biological agent/toxin listed as a select agent. The Act establishes criminal penalties and access restrictions; recipients must comply with related select agent regulations and access controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility/Qualification Reporting in SAM.gov (NDAA 2013 / 2 CFR App XII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients with currently active Federal awards and cumulative total value > $10,000,000 must report and maintain information in SAM.gov about civil, criminal, and administrative proceedings reaching final disposition within the most recent five-year period and make semi-annual disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings information will be public in the designated integrity and performance system. Full reporting requirements/procedures are in Appendix XII to 2 CFR Part 200.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Disclosures (2 CFR 200.113)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants, recipients, or subrecipients must promptly disclose in writing to the NIH awarding IC, the HHS OIG, and pass-through entity whenever they have credible evidence of a violation of Federal criminal law in connection with the Federal award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covered violations include fraud, conflict of interest, bribery, gratuity violations in Title 18, or violations of the civil False Claims Act (31 U.S.C. 3729–3733). Disclosures must be sent in writing to the NIH CGMO listed on the NoA and to the HHS OIG (address, URL, and email provided). Failure to disclose can lead to remedies described in 2 CFR Part 200.339 and enforcement actions including suspension or debarment under applicable statutes/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never Contract with the Enemy (2 CFR Part 183)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations implementing 'Never Contract with the Enemy' apply to covered contracts, grants, and cooperative agreements that meet certain thresholds and contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to awards expected to exceed $50,000, performed outside the United States/territories, and in support of a contingency operation with members of the Armed Forces actively engaged in hostilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Equipment or Services (Section 889 / Pub. L. 115-232)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients and subrecipients are prohibited from using loan or grant funds to procure, extend/renew contracts for, or enter contracts for 'covered telecommunications equipment or services.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Covered telecommunications equipment or services' includes: (1) equipment produced by Huawei or ZTE (or subsidiaries/affiliates); (2) video surveillance/telecom equipment produced by Hytera, Hikvision, or Dahua for specified national security purposes; (3) telecom or video surveillance services provided by such entities or using such equipment; and (4) equipment/services produced/provided by entities reasonably believed (by Secretary of Defense in consultation with DNI/FBI) to be owned/controlled by or connected to the government of a covered foreign country (defined as the People's Republic of China). Also includes systems that use such equipment/services as a substantial/essential component or critical technology. In implementing the prohibition, agency heads must prioritize assistance to help affected entities transition away from covered equipment and procure replacements. Acceptance of a loan/grant certifies compliance with the prohibition; recipients are not required to repeatedly certify beyond acceptance and payment request/financial report certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whistleblower Protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees of recipients/subrecipients must not be retaliated against for disclosing information they reasonably believe evidences gross mismanagement, gross waste, abuse of authority, substantial/specific danger to public health or safety, or violations of law/regulation related to a Federal contract or grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients and subrecipients must inform employees in writing of employee whistleblower rights and protections under 41 U.S.C. 4712. See statutory whistleblower protections at 10 U.S.C. 4701, 41 U.S.C. 4712, 41 U.S.C. 4304, and 10 U.S.C. 4310.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of Federal Funding (Steven's Amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must acknowledge Federal funding when issuing statements, press releases, RFPs, bid invitations, and other documents describing projects or programs funded in whole or in part with Federal money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are required to state (1) the percentage and dollar amounts of total program/project costs financed with Federal money and (2) the dollar amount of total costs financed by nongovernmental sources, but the second requirement applies only for NIH programs that require cost-sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Dissemination of False or Deliberately Misleading Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds made available in the governing appropriations Act may not be used to disseminate information that is deliberately false or misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an appropriation-level restriction applicable to funded activities and communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gun Control Appropriation Restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH funds may not be used, in whole or in part, to advocate or promote gun control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition applies to advocacy or promotion of gun control; see related lobbying/appropriation prohibitions for scope and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Embryo Research and Cloning Ban
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH funds may not be used to (1) create a human embryo or embryos for research purposes or (2) conduct research in which a human embryo(s) are destroyed, discarded, or knowingly subjected to risk of injury or death greater than that allowed for research on fetuses in utero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term 'human embryo or embryos' includes organisms derived from human gametes or human diploid cells by fertilization, parthenogenesis, cloning, or other means, and not protected as human subjects under 45 CFR Part 46, as of enactment. Additionally, per NIH Director statement (April 28, 2015), NIH will not fund any use of gene-editing technologies in human embryos. Presidential memorandum (March 4, 1997) prohibits use of Federal funds for cloning of human beings. Applicable citations: 45 CFR Part 46.204(b), subsection 498(b) of the PHS Act (42 U.S.C.289g(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lobbying—Appropriation Prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriated NIH funds may not be used for activities designed to influence the enactment of legislation (or certain regulations/administrative actions) before Congress or State/local legislatures, except for normal and recognized executive-legislative relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits use of funds for preparation/distribution/use of kits, pamphlets, publications, electronic communications, radio/TV/video presentations designed to support or defeat legislation, except when presented to the Congress or State legislature itself or in normal executive-legislative relations. No part of any appropriations Act shall pay salaries/expenses of any recipient or agent related to activity designed to influence legislation, appropriations, regulation, administrative action, or Executive Order, except as described. Also bars use of funds to advocate/promote proposed/pending/future tax increases or restrictions on legal consumer products (including gun control), with limited exceptions. See related Public Policy Requirements—Lobbying Prohibition and Appropriation Mandates—Gun Control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion or Legalization of Controlled Substances Restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are prohibited from knowingly using appropriated funds to support activities that promote legalization of any Schedule I drug or other controlled substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: Limitation does not apply if the recipient notifies the GMO that there is significant medical evidence of a therapeutic advantage to the substance's use or that federally sponsored clinical trials are being conducted to determine therapeutic advantage. See also Controlled Substances policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on Abortion Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH appropriated funds (and funds in any trust fund to which funds are appropriated) may not be spent for any abortion nor for health benefits coverage that includes coverage of abortion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: 'health benefits coverage' = package of services covered by a managed care provider or organization under contract/arrangement. Exceptions (4.2.7.1): (A) abortion if pregnancy resulted from rape or incest, or if woman's life is endangered as certified by physician; (B) does not prohibit expenditure of State/local/private funds (other than Medicaid matching funds); (C) does not restrict managed care providers or States/localities from offering abortion coverage paid for with State funds; (D) none of NIH funds may be made available to an agency/program/government that discriminates against health care entities that do not provide/pay for/refer for abortions (includes physicians, hospitals, providers, insurers, or other health care entities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on Distribution of Sterile Needles
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH appropriated funds may not be used to carry out programs distributing sterile needles/syringes for hypodermic injection of illegal drugs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: Limitation does not apply to elements of a program other than making such purchases if the relevant State/local health department, in consultation with CDC, determines the jurisdiction is experiencing or at risk for a significant increase in hepatitis infections or an HIV outbreak due to injection drug use, and such program operates in accordance with State/local law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary Cap / Salary Limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds may not be used to pay direct or indirect salaries through a grant at a rate in excess of that prescribed in the governing appropriations Act (legislative salary limitation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications reflecting higher salaries will be adjusted; recipients may not draw down funds to pay salaries above the rate limitation. Recipients must have policies/procedures consistently applied regardless of funding source. Current/historical salary cap info is on NIH Salary Cap Summary page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction of Pornography on Computer Networks
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds may not be used to maintain or establish a computer network unless such network blocks viewing, downloading, and exchanging of pornography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: does not limit use of funds necessary for Federal/State/tribal/local law enforcement agencies or other entities carrying out criminal investigations, prosecution, or adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on Requesting Political Affiliation for Federal Scientific Advisory Committee Candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds may not be used to request that a candidate for appointment to a Federal scientific advisory committee disclose political affiliation or voting history or positions not directly related to and necessary for the committee's work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This stems from Section 515 of the FY2014 Consolidated Appropriations Act; the restriction applies to funds used to request such disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Award (NoA) as Legal Document
rubrics_metrics.description: The NoA is the legal document notifying the recipient that an award has been made and that funds may be requested; it is issued for the initial budget period and each subsequent budget period and reflects future-year commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A revised NoA may be issued to change period/amount/terms. NIH will not issue a revised NoA to reflect recipient post-award rebudgeting. Costs incurred before the initial NoA are at the applicant's risk. The NoA provides standardized page one data elements and remainder sections (Award Data, Payment Info, Applicable Terms/Conditions). Acceptance of the NoA is indicated by drawing/requesting funds from the designated payment system; if the recipient cannot accept the award it must notify the GMO immediately. Once accepted, the NoA contents are binding unless modified by a revised NoA.

rubrics_metrics.name: NoA Standardized Page One Data Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS standardized page one of the NoA contains specified data elements required for all discretionary awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements include: HHS Operating Division; Federal Award Identification Number; Federal Award Date; Recipient Information (name, congressional district, payment system identifier, EIN, DUNS/UEI); Project Director/PI; Authorized Official; Federal Agency Info; Awarding Agency Contact Info; Program Official Contact Info; Federal Award Info (award number, UF Award ID, statutory authority, project title, Assistance Listing Number/CFDA); Award Action Type; Is this Award R&D?; Summary Federal Award Financial Info (budget period dates, total federal funds obligated by action, direct cost, indirect cost, authorized carryover, offset, total funds obligated this budget period, total approved cost sharing/matching where applicable, total federal and non-federal approved this budget period, project period start/end, total amount of federal award including approved cost sharing/matching this project period, authorized treatment of program income); Grants Management Officer signature; Remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: NoA Remainder Information and Terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond page one, the NoA includes Award Data (cumulative approved budget, anticipated future-year commitments, cognizant contacts, indirect cost rate, applicable terms/conditions), Payment Information, and Sections III/IV of applicable terms/conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May reference participation in Federal Demonstration Partnership (FDP) if applicable. The auditor should identify NIH awards as part of the R&D cluster for SEFA; auditors need not report classification disconnects unless indirect costs are charged at a different rate than award specifies.

rubrics_metrics.name: NoA Notification and eRA Commons Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH notifies recipient organizations via e-mail when an award has been issued; the NoA is made available in eRA Commons Status module and eRA Commons is the official repository for the NoA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations must register a valid NoA notification e-mail in the eRA Commons Institutional Profile (preferably an address not tied to an individual). Recipients are responsible for maintaining current and accurate e-mail addresses; NIH will not distribute NoAs other than through the system-generated e-mail notification process. Recipients without a current NoA e-mail must access NoAs via eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated Applications/Awards Coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: When projects/programs are funded by multiple associated awards, the NoA will document coordination requirements, including any reporting requirements to be coordinated in future years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to initiatives where multiple awards are issued at different institutions; specific terms and conditions will document coordination among recipient institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding: Project Period System and Determination of Project Length
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH commonly uses a project period funding system: projects are approved programmatically for the entire planned period but funded in annual budget periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Length of initial project period or subsequent competitive segment is determined by statutory/regulatory requirements, applicant-requested length, peer reviewer recommendations, awarding IC programmatic determination of review frequency, and NIH funding principles. Policy limits each competitive segment to a maximum of 5 years (exclusive of non-competing extensions). Single awards covering entire period generally used only for construction/modernization, total planned support <18 months, or special support mechanisms. Initial NoA provides funds for the first budget period, budget periods usually are 12 months (shorter/longer may be established for compelling reasons). NoA indicates projected future-year funding which is contingent on satisfactory progress, availability of funds, and federal interests — not guarantees. Recipients must submit annual progress reports (RPPR) as prerequisite to approval/funding of subsequent budget periods. All agencies required by 31 U.S.C. §1552(a) to close fixed year appropriation accounts and cancel balances by Sept 30 of the fifth fiscal year after year of availability; recipients must report disbursements on FFR by Aug 31 of the fifth fiscal year to avoid carryover limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Presentation and Rebudgeting Flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Each NoA sets forth the amount of funds awarded, shown either as categorical (line item) budget or as total direct costs and indirect costs; modular awards are without categorical budgets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients have certain rebudgeting flexibility within overall awarded amount (see Changes in Project and Budget). Recipients may be required to provide matching funds under construction awards or other NIH programs if specified in the NOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of Additional or Special Terms and Conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH may add program-specific or award-specific terms and conditions in addition to or in lieu of standard terms if warranted by programmatic or recipient performance/management concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If GMO finds recipient's management systems/practices inadequate to ensure stewardship of funds or achieve award objectives, NIH may impose more restrictive terms (per 42 CFR Part 52.9, 2 CFR 200.339, 45 CFR Part 75.371), e.g., require prior approval for ordinarily unrestricted expenditures, require more frequent reports, closer monitoring, or provide assistance to take corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment Method and Cash Management (PMS rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS Payment Management System (PMS) administers grants payment; payments may be made by several advance payment methods and are generally advance payments under NIH grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments are made in accordance with Treasury and OMB requirements (2 CFR Part 200.305) intended to minimize time between Federal transfer and recipient disbursement. Recipients should draw funds on an as-needed basis—specifically, no more than 3 business days before funds are needed. Payment method examples: SMARTLINK II/ACH, cash request, reimbursement basis as specified on the NoA.
